youtube.title: Why Are Stop Signs Octagons? (And Why They Used to Be Yellow)
youtube.description:
Eight sides, red and white: the stop sign is the only octagon on American roads. That's on purpose. In 1923 a group of highway officials gave every sign shape a meaning, with one simple rule: the more sides, the bigger the danger.

From Detroit's first white square stop sign in 1915 to the circle saved for railroad crossings, why you can read a stop sign from behind or under snow, and why stop signs were yellow until 1954: this is the hidden why behind the stop sign.

- MUTCD 1954 edition: stop signs changed to red with white letters
